questions.q: What does the speaker say he will not do until Zion’s righteousness shines out?
questions.a: He says he will not be silent or quiet.

questions.q: Who will see Zion’s righteousness and glory?
questions.a: The nations will see Zion’s righteousness, and all the kings will see her glory.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do to show he is proud of Zion, according to this verse?
questions.a: He shows Zion off proudly, like a king might hold out his beautiful crown for people to admire.

questions.q: What will no longer be said of Zion and her land?
questions.a: Zion will no longer be called “Abandoned,” and her land will no longer be called “Devastation.”

questions.q: Why will Zion be called “My Delight is in Her” and her land “Married”?
questions.a: She will be called those things because Yahweh delights in her, and her land will be married.

questions.q: Who will be as happy about Zion as a bridegroom is about his bride?
questions.a: Zion’s God will be as happy about her as a bridegroom is about his bride.

questions.q: Why have watchmen been put on the walls of Jerusalem?
questions.a: They are put there to keep reminding Yahweh, giving him no rest, until he restores Jerusalem and makes people throughout the earth admire the city.

questions.q: What has Yahweh sworn by his own great power?
questions.a: He has sworn that he will never again let enemies take away Jerusalem’s grain, and that foreigners will never again drink her new wine.

questions.q: Who will eat the grain and praise Yahweh?
questions.a: Those who harvest the grain will eat it themselves and praise Yahweh, and those who gather the grapes will drink the wine in the courts of Yahweh’s temple.

questions.q: What are the people commanded to do to prepare the way for others to return?
questions.a: They are commanded to go out through the city gates, prepare the road, build up the highway, clear away the stones, and raise a signal flag.

questions.q: What does Yahweh announce to the ends of the earth?
questions.a: Yahweh announces, “Tell the people of Jerusalem, ‘Pay attention! The one who saves you is coming! He is bringing with him the people he has rescued from your enemies.’”

questions.q: What new names will people give to Jerusalem and its people?
questions.a: People will call them “the holy people” and “the people Yahweh has redeemed.” They will call Jerusalem “the city Yahweh cares for” and “the city that is not abandoned.”

commentary.text: God's care of his church and people. (Is. 62:1-5) The office of ministers in preaching the gospel. (Is. 62:6-9) Every hinderance shall be removed from the way of salvation. (Is. 62:10-12)

Is. 62:1-5 The Son of God here assures his church of his unfailing love, and his pleading for her under all trails and difficulties. She shall be called by a new name, a pleasant name, such as she was never called by before. The state of true religion in the world, before the preaching of the gospel, no man seemed to have any real concern for. God, by his grace, has wrought that in his church, which makes her his delight. Let us thence learn motives to holiness. If the Lord rejoices over us, we should rejoice in his service.

Is. 62:6-9 God's professing people must be a praying people. He is not displeased with us for being earnest, as men commonly are; he bids us to cry after him, and give him no rest, Luke 11:5,6. It is a sign that God is coming to a people in mercy, when he pours out a spirit of prayer upon them. See how uncertain our creature-comforts are. See also God's mercy in giving plenty, and peace to enjoy it. Let us delight in attending the courts of the Lord, that we may enjoy the consolations of his Spirit.

Is. 62:10-12 Way shall be made for Christ's salvation; all difficulties shall be removed. He brings a reward of comfort and peace with him; but a work of humiliation and reformation before him; and they shall be called, The holy people, and, The redeemed of the Lord. Holiness puts honour and beauty upon any place or person, makes them admired, beloved, and sought after. Many events may have been part fulfilments of this, as earnests of more glorious times yet to come. The close connexion between the blessedness of the Jews and of the Gentiles, runs through the Scriptures. The Lord Jesus will complete his work, and he never will forsake one whom he has redeemed and sanctified.
